Warning: Files deleted with the new shredder cannot be recovered by any data recovery tool or forensic software.
Normally when you delete a photo on an Android phone, the system only erases the file\'s name—the photo itself stays on your device\'s memory chip where recovery apps can easily bring it back.

Imava now includes a Cryptographic Secure Shredder. When you permanently delete photos or empty the trash, Imava physically overwrites your photo\'s memory blocks with random scrambled data and zeroes before deleting it.

• Impossible to undelete: Photos are destroyed completely.\n• Large files (e.g. 4K videos) may take an extra second to physically wipe.\n• You can toggle this setting anytime under Settings > Privacy & Security.
Streams cryptographic pseudo-random bytes (via SecureRandom) in 64KB buffers across all allocated clusters in synchronous \'rws\' mode.
Obliterates JPEG (FF D8), PNG, MP4 (ftyp), and EXIF headers with 0x00 bytes to defeat raw sector carving tools (DiskDigger, PhotoRec).
Executes FileDescriptor.sync() and FileChannel.force(true) to flush hardware controller caches, truncates file to 0 bytes, scrambles filename to UUID.tmp, and unlinks inode.
